title: Lucid Assay Pipeline Lifecycle Attestation Predicate v1
description: In-toto predicate carried inside a DSSE-wrapped in-toto Statement (predicateType = this $id). Captures VCS provenance, supply-chain artifact identity, test verification, coverage, assertion-quality heuristics, and the derived Release Confidence Score (RCS) for a single CI pipeline run.

predicate_version.description: Schema/predicate semantic version, pinned per attestation for forward-compatible verification.

base_commit_sha.description: Merge-base commit against the target branch, used for patch coverage diffing. Null when unavailable (e.g. push to default branch, shallow clone with no base).

approvers.description: Handles of reviewers who approved, deduplicated, as of attestation time.

commit_author.description: Live GitHub commit-author identity check (cli/parsers/commit_author.py): whether the commit's author resolves to a linked, verified GitHub account (GitHub's own `author.login`, distinct from the trivially-spoofable free-text git author name/email). Null when not collected (e.g. off-CI, no GITHUB_TOKEN, or an attestation predating this field) -- absence must not be read as verified.

commit_signature_verified.description: A genuinely stronger claim than verified_github_account: whether this exact commit carries a cryptographic signature (GPG/SSH) GitHub itself verified. Null when not determined -- unavailable, not captured, or a GitHub-web-flow merge/squash/rebase walk-back that exhausted its hop limit -- never treated as a confirmed pass. See cli/parsers/commit_author.py's module docstring for the merge/squash/rebase walk-back this reflects.

commit_signature_type.description: Inferred from the raw PEM signature header (e.g. "gpg"/"ssh") since GitHub's commits API exposes no parsed key-ID/fingerprint field. Null when no signature was evaluated.

commit_signature_source_sha.description: The commit whose own signature this verdict actually describes. Null when the originally-requested commit's own signature was evaluated directly; set to a different SHA when that commit was a GitHub-web-flow-generated merge/squash/rebase commit and this walked back to the real pre-merge branch tip instead.

branch_governance.description: Live GitHub branch-governance check (cli/parsers/github_rules.py): whether the target branch would actually let this change land unreviewed, independent of this PR's own approval state. A top-level predicate field, always present (not nested under vcs).

reason_code.description: Machine-readable classification of a specific known available=false cause (e.g. platform_unsupported_tier). Null/absent for every other case -- must not be inferred as a generic failure.

required_status_check_contexts.description: The `context` of every required_status_checks rule entry applying to this branch (e.g. "ci/lucid-assay-verify"). Absent/empty on attestations predating this field, or whenever available=false.

linear_history_required.description: Whether a 'required_linear_history' rule is active on the branch (merge commits disallowed -- squash/rebase only). Absent on attestations predating this field, or whenever available=false.

force_pushes_blocked.description: Whether a 'non_fast_forward' rule is active on the branch (history rewrite via force-push disallowed). Absent on attestations predating this field, or whenever available=false.

deletions_blocked.description: Whether a 'deletion' rule is active on the branch (branch deletion disallowed). Absent on attestations predating this field, or whenever available=false.

repository_governance.description: Repository/workstation-hygiene compensating controls (cli/parsers/github_rules.py, cli/parsers/commit_author.py) for a solo-maintained repo that structurally can't satisfy SLSA Source Level 4's two-party review -- see cli/verify.py's Repository & Workstation Governance section. Deliberately separate from vcs (SLSA Build/Source reads) and branch_governance (S2C2F/RCS governance scoring reads): this project's own policy assessment, not a claim about either ratified/draft specification.

commit_signature.description: Null when no commit_author was collected at all (e.g. off-CI, no GITHUB_TOKEN, or an attestation predating this field) -- absence must not be read as verified.

verified.description: Whether source_sha's own commit.verification.verified came back true. Null when not captured, or when a GitHub-web-flow merge commit walk-back (see below) failed partway through -- distinct from a confirmed-unsigned commit, which is false.

reason.description: GitHub's own commit.verification.reason (e.g. 'valid', 'unsigned', 'bad_signature') for source_sha, or a walk-back failure explanation when verified is null because the walk-back itself failed.

signature_type.description: Inferred from source_sha's own raw signature blob PEM-style header. Null when no signature is present or its header isn't recognized.

source_sha.description: The commit whose own signature this verdict actually describes. Null when the originally-requested commit's own signature was evaluated directly; set to a different SHA when that commit was a GitHub-web-flow-generated merge commit (auto-signed by GitHub's own key on every PR merge, regardless of the author's own signing setup) and this walked back to the PR's real head commit instead -- see cli/parsers/commit_author.py's docstring.

name.description: OCI image ref or artifact name, e.g. registry/org/svc

uri.description: Content-addressed WORM storage URI, e.g. s3://evidence/sha256/<hash>

component_count.description: Number of components cli.parsers.sbom extracted from this SBOM

met.description: Real, zero-tolerance gate: true only when tests > 0 and failed == 0 and errored == 0 and skipped == 0. Not derived from a configurable minimum -- any failure, error, or skip means false.

flaky_retries.description: Count of test cases that failed at least once then passed on retry within this run.

available.description: False when base_commit_sha is unavailable or diff yields zero coverable changed lines.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable classification of a specific known available=false cause (e.g. no_coverable_lines). Null/absent for every other case.

real.description: Vanity-test-aware coverage (see $defs/realCoverageTrack); absent on an attestation predating this field.

density_ratio.description: assertions / test_functions; null when total_test_functions is 0.

target.description: cli/scorer.py's ASSERTION_DENSITY_TARGET, verbatim -- a fixed constant, not a per-run CLI flag. Absent on attestations predating this field.

met.description: True only when density_ratio is real and >= target -- a genuine, unconditional gate (no --min-assertion-density flag exists to make this configurable). False, never fabricated true, when density_ratio is null. Absent on attestations predating this field.

valid_test_functions.description: Non-skipped test functions with at least one real (non-tautological) assertion -- total_test_functions minus "vanity" tests (an empty body, or one whose only assertions are tautological, e.g. `assert True`). Absent on attestations predating this field.

valid_test_ratio.description: valid_test_functions / total_test_functions; null when total_test_functions is 0. Absent on attestations predating this field.

empty_test_bodies.description: Test functions with zero assertions and zero meaningful statements.

assertion_only_true.description: Suspicious tautological assertions, e.g. assert True / expect(true).toBe(true).

ast_skipped_test_functions.description: Test functions the AST engine identified as skipped/disabled (e.g. @Disabled, it.skip, t.Skip-wholesale, @unittest.skip*) across every scanned language; excluded from total_test_functions/total_assertions.

languages.description: Per-language breakdown of the AST assertion engine's scan, keyed by language id (python, typescript, javascript, go, java). Absent/empty on older attestations predating multi-language support.

static_analysis.description: SARIF 2.1.0 static-analysis findings (see cli/parsers/sarif.py), differential-scored against the patch. configured=false means no --sarif input was given at all for this run (available is then always false too -- nothing was ever evaluated, so there's no real result to call available); configured=true, available=false means a --sarif input was given but couldn't be read/parsed (see reasons); configured=true, available=true is a real, completed scan (findings/tools populated, possibly empty). Absent entirely on attestations predating this feature; configured absent (available alone present) on an attestation predating the configured/available split (lucid-assay PR #47) -- available=true there is ambiguous between "never configured" and "genuinely clean scan", by that earlier schema's own now-corrected mistake.

configured.description: True iff --sarif was passed at least once for this run. False means static analysis was never invoked -- not skipped/bypassed after being requested, just never asked for.

patch_errors_count.description: Findings at level=error whose file/line intersects the diff's changed lines -- weighed far more heavily by the scorer than a pre-existing baseline finding.

critical_count.description: Findings whose rule carries a properties["security-severity"] (the GitHub code-scanning SARIF convention several scanners populate, e.g. Grype/CodeQL/Snyk) mapping to a Critical CVSS band (>=9.0). Independent of errors_count/warnings_count/etc., which bucket by the SARIF spec's own coarser `level` -- a tool like Grype maps both Critical and High to level=error, so this is the only way to tell them apart.

reasons.description: Human-readable causes when available=false (e.g. an unreadable/corrupt --sarif input); aggregation fails closed, so any one bad input taints the whole report.

tools.description: Per-tool breakdown: driver metadata, rule-ID/category/tag grouping, a raw-report integrity hash, and an extensible bag for tool-specific enrichments (e.g. SonarQube quality gate). Concatenated across multiple --sarif inputs, one entry per (file, tool) pair -- each keeps its own file's report_hash rather than being merged across files.

rules.description: Findings for this tool, grouped by rule ID.

extensions.description: Tool-specific metadata not part of the core SARIF result shape, e.g. SonarQube's quality gate or complexity/debt metrics -- sourced from a SARIF run's own properties bag, or merged in externally via --sonar-metrics for a scanner that doesn't embed them.

report_hash.description: SHA-256 of the raw SARIF file this tool's results were parsed from.

resolved_dependencies.description: Pinned/resolved dependencies detected from lockfiles under the repo (cli/parsers/lockfiles.py: uv.lock, package-lock.json, go.sum, Gradle/Maven locks), deduplicated by uri. Empty when no recognized lockfile was found under the repo, or on attestations predating this field. Distinct from -- and not a substitute for -- SLSA v1.0 provenance's buildDefinition.resolvedDependencies, which lives on a differently-shaped predicate entirely.

uri.description: A pkg: PURL identifying the resolved dependency, e.g. pkg:pypi/requests@2.31.0.

digest.description: algorithm -> hex digest map, e.g. {"sha256": "..."}. Empty when the lockfile format carries no cryptographic digest (Gradle/Maven) or it couldn't be decoded.

s2c2f.description: S2C2F (Secure Supply Chain Consumption Framework) control evaluation (cli/parsers/s2c2f.py) -- only the subset of the published catalog this pipeline can honestly assess from a real signal; every unsupported control id is simply absent from controls[], never fabricated as met/unmet. controls[] is empty on attestations predating this field, or when S2C2F evaluation was skipped for this run.

status.description: "not_yet_reported" means evaluation could not be completed (no token, network/auth failure, or no generic signal exists for this control) -- never conflated with "unmet" (evaluation succeeded and found the control unsatisfied).

static_analysis.description: Not in `required`: absent on attestations predating the SARIF static-analysis component (cli/scorer.py WEIGHTS).

mutation_testing.description: Not in `required`: absent on attestations predating cli/mutation.py. Retired `assertion_integrity`'s slot -- weight is always 0.0 by construction, since this component discounts the test_health/patch_coverage/overall_coverage cluster via release_confidence_score.mutation_multiplier rather than adding its own weighted share; weighted_score here carries the signed point delta the multiplier caused (can legitimately be negative -- see $defs/mutationScoreComponent, distinct from the generic scoreComponent every other component uses). See predicate.mutation_testing for the full detail (scoped_files, top_surviving_mutants) this compact form doesn't carry.

degraded.description: True if any component fell back to a penalized default due to missing/unavailable input data.

degraded_reasons.description: Which independent trigger(s) caused degraded=true (e.g. no_pr_context, sarif_unavailable, a namespaced branch_governance:<reason_code> / patch_coverage:<reason_code> / mutation_testing:<reason_code>). Empty when degraded=false. Absent/malformed on an attestation predating this field -- cli/verify.py's --disallow-degraded treats that as non-exempt.

mutation_multiplier.description: The multiplier release_confidence_score.value's test_health/patch_coverage/overall_coverage subtotal was discounted by (1.0 = no discount). Absent on attestations predating cli/mutation.py.

pre_multiplier_cluster_score.description: The test_health/patch_coverage/overall_coverage weighted subtotal *before* mutation_multiplier was applied -- lets an auditor reconstruct the discount rather than reverse-engineering it from value alone. Absent on attestations predating cli/mutation.py.

mutation_testing.description: Diff-scoped mutation testing over the source lines actually changed in this run's diff -- Python (mutmut), TypeScript/JavaScript (Stryker), and Java (PIT), combined by cli/mutation's dispatcher into one score (see `by_language` for the per-language breakdown) -- the real signal release_confidence_score.components.mutation_testing's multiplier is derived from. Absent on attestations predating this field.

available.description: False when mutation testing genuinely wasn't evaluated (no source changes in a supported language, no tool configured for any language touched, or the caller opted out) -- distinct from a real run that found nothing to discount.

mutation_score.description: killed / (killed + survived) * 100, summed across every language that actually ran; null when it couldn't be computed (no mutants tested, or killed+survived=0).

tested.description: killed + survived + timeout -- the real sample size, distinct from total_generated.

total_generated.description: Every mutant the tool(s) generated across their configured scope, including ones never selected for testing this run -- not the sample size; see `tested`.

scoped_files.description: Every file, across every language, this run's diff touched and mutation-tested against.

line.description: Python: best-effort AST lookup of the function's own definition. TypeScript/JavaScript (Stryker) and Java (PIT): the tool's own reported line number, real ground truth, not a locator. The diff/description text, not this field alone, is the primary evidence for a surviving mutant.

diff.description: Python: the real unified diff mutmut produced for this mutant, verbatim. TypeScript/JavaScript: the tool's own mutatorName + replacement value. Java: PIT's own mutator class + human description (e.g. "changed conditional boundary"). Go: gremlins' own mutation type + file:line:column. Real ground truth in every case, never a taxonomy label the tool itself doesn't expose.

by_language.description: Per-language breakdown (killed/survived/timeout/total_generated/scoped_files) for every language that actually ran -- mirrors assertion_density.languages' own per-language precedent. A language with no tool configured in this repo, or that had no changed files in this diff, is simply absent here (never a fabricated zero). Absent/empty on attestations predating this field, or a single-language run that never populated it.

reason.description: Human/auditor-readable justification, e.g. 'zero tests executed', 'patch coverage unavailable, fell back to overall*0.7'.

available.description: False when this control was never actually evaluated for this run (e.g. static_analysis with no --sarif configured) -- raw_score/weighted_score still carry the scoring policy's baseline (never penalizing an opt-in control that wasn't asked to run), but a consumer must not read that baseline number as a real measurement. True for every component that ran a real check, whether it passed or not.

mutationScoreComponent.description: Same shape as scoreComponent, except weighted_score is a signed delta ((multiplier - 1.0) * the test_health/patch_coverage/overall_coverage cluster's own weighted subtotal), not a 0-100 weighted share -- mutation_testing discounts that cluster rather than adding its own additive weight (weight is always 0.0 here, by construction). Confirmed empirically (a real end-to-end run) that reusing scoreComponent's weighted_score minimum:0 constraint here falsely flags a legitimate negative discount as a schema violation.

realCoverageTrack.description: One track (overall or patch) of vanity-test-aware coverage (cli.real_coverage): measured_line_rate is the same rate coverage.overall/patch.line_rate already reports over this same line set; real_line_rate subtracts lines covered only by tests the AST engine flags as vanity (zero real assertions) from the numerator, same denominator. available=false (with a reason) when --coverage-contexts wasn't provided, the export was malformed, or -- for the patch track specifically -- no patch-modified-lines data was available.

vanity_only_lines.description: Lines counted covered in measured_line_rate whose every attributed covering test is vanity -- discounted from real_line_rate's numerator.
